If A and B are the domain and range of a real valued function $f(x) = \dfrac{|x|}{\sqrt{1 - |x|}}$, then $A \cup B =$
solution:
Domain: $1 - |x| > 0 \Rightarrow A = (-1, 1)$.

Range: with $t = |x| \in [0, 1)$, $y = \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{1-t}}$ is increasing from 0 to $\infty$, so $B = [0, \infty)$.

$A \cup B = (-1, \infty)$

Let a point $P$ in the Argand plane represent the complex number $z$. If $\arg\left(\dfrac{2z - i}{z - 2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then the locus of $P$ is
solution:
$\dfrac{2z - i}{z - 2} = \dfrac{2x^2 + 2y^2 - 4x - y}{(x-2)^2 + y^2} + i\,\dfrac{-x - 4y + 2}{(x-2)^2 + y^2}$

$\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1 \Rightarrow$ Imaginary part = Real part:

$-x - 4y + 2 = 2x^2 + 2y^2 - 4x - y \Rightarrow 2x^2 + 2y^2 - 3x + 3y - 2 = 0$
